proposals.before: The Book of Changes, Kun, first six lines, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”
proposals.after: The Book of Changes, Kun, first yin line, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”
proposals.reason: 初六 is the first yin line of hexagram Kun, not “first six lines.”

proposals.before: The Family, first nine lines, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”
proposals.after: The Family, first yang line, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”
proposals.reason: 初九 is the first yang line of hexagram Jiaren, not “first nine lines.”

proposals.before: Taizu said: “Father Zhu the Classicist studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”
proposals.after: Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”
proposals.reason: 朱五經 is an epithet “Zhu of the Five Classics,” not “Father Zhu the Classicist.”

proposals.before: Taizu said: “Zhu the Fifth Classicist read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”
proposals.after: Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”
proposals.reason: 五經 names the Five Classics, not an ordinal “Fifth.”

proposals.before: In the autumn of Dazhun 2 the empress fell ill; augurs said she must go home.”
proposals.after: In the autumn of Dashun 2 the empress fell ill; augurs said she must go home.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun (AD 891), not “Dazhun”; the idiomatic field also has a stray closing quote.

proposals.before: In autumn of the second year of Dazhun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”
proposals.after: In autumn of the second year of Dashun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”
proposals.reason: 大順 is the Tang Dashun reign, conventionally Dashun, not Dazhun.

proposals.before: Taizu betrothed her in his youth; she bore Youzhen, the Last Emperor.
proposals.after: Taizu betrothed her in his youth; she bore the Last Emperor.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names only 末帝; “Youzhen” is an invented personal name not in this unit.

proposals.before: In Jin Tianfu 3 an edict allowed families to reclaim criminal heads held at the altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released, and Right Palace Gate General An Chongruan buried it with the consort.
proposals.after: In Jin Tianfu 3 an edict allowed families to reclaim criminal heads held at the altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released, and General of the Right Guard An Chongruan buried it with the consort.
proposals.reason: 右衛將軍 is General of the Right Guard, not “Right Palace Gate General.”

proposals.before: Eight sons by blood: Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.
proposals.after: Eight sons: the eldest Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.
proposals.reason: 八子 lists seven blood sons plus one adopted son; “eight sons by blood” invents an eighth biological son.

proposals.before: Once, as Taizu drank and diced with him in the palace, Quanyu, deep in wine, hurled the dice against the bowl and shouted: “Zhu the Third, you were a dirt farmer from Dangshan until heaven made you lord of four circuits—what did the throne ever owe you?”?
proposals.after: Once, as Taizu drank and diced with him in the palace, Quanyu, deep in wine, hurled the dice against the bowl and shouted: “Zhu the Third, you were a dirt farmer from Dangshan until heaven made you lord of four circuits—what did the throne ever owe you?”
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English ends with a stray extra question mark after the closing quote.

proposals.after: Cun’s sons were Youning and Youlun.

proposals.before: Cui Yin sent envoys to halt him, but Taizu was convinced that Yin and his circle had murdered Youlun. He demanded their deaths; Zhaozong refused. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui of Henan, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
proposals.after: Cui Yin sent envoys to halt him, but Taizu was convinced that Yin and his circle had murdered Youlun. He demanded their deaths; Zhaozong refused. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
proposals.reason: 京兆尹 is the metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, not “of Henan.”

proposals.before: He served as acting prefect of Xuzhou.
proposals.after: He served as acting prefect of Xu.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州 Xuzhou; the idiomatic field conflates the two.
